That the Rocky Mountains rose higher than the Appalachian hills

trap_notes.b: The Missouri does flow into the Mississippi; the expedition started at St. Louis.
trap_notes.c: Lewis and Clark interacted with dozens of Plains and Plateau nations.
trap_notes.d: The expedition confirmed the Rockies were far higher and wider than expected.
trap_notes.default: The rugged Continental Divide proved no simple river shortcut linked the oceans.

prompt: Why has Ethiopia's Grand Renaissance Dam sparked diplomatic tension with downstream Egypt?

options.text: Egypt relies almost entirely on the Nile for water and fears reduced flow
The dam blocks Mediterranean oil tankers from entering the Suez Canal
Ethiopia plans to pump Red Sea saltwater upstream into Cairo
Egypt receives heavy monsoon rains and fears flooding from the dam

explanation: Because the Blue Nile supplies most of the Nile's flow, upstream dam management directly affects Egyptian farming and cities.

trap_notes.b: The dam sits thousands of miles upstream in Ethiopia, far from Suez.
trap_notes.c: The project is a freshwater hydroelectric dam, not a saltwater pipeline.
trap_notes.d: Egypt is hyper-arid and depends on steady Nile water, not local monsoon rain.
trap_notes.default: Downstream arid nations depend heavily on upstream river management.

prompt: Why do rapid rural-to-urban migrants in developing countries often settle in informal peri-urban districts?

options.text: City jobs draw newcomers faster than formal housing and transit expand
Municipal laws require factory workers to camp outside city utilities
Rural farm wages are double the pay of urban manufacturing jobs
Central business districts lack any electricity or paved roads

explanation: When millions move to cities for work, affordable formal housing lags behind, creating self-built neighborhoods on urban fringes.

trap_notes.b: Informal settlements arise from housing shortages and poverty, not mandates.
trap_notes.c: Higher expected urban wages are a primary pull factor for migrants.
trap_notes.d: Central districts have dense infrastructure, which makes central land unaffordable.
trap_notes.default: Rapid urban migration outpaces affordable housing and utility construction.

prompt: How does California's Mediterranean climate make the Central Valley a top U.S. fruit and nut producer?

options.text: Dry sunny summers curb crop fungus while winter mountain snow irrigates
Daily summer thunderstorms keep orchard soils flooded all July
Subzero winter blizzards kill all orchard pests across the valley floor
High coastal humidity ripens citrus without any irrigation canals

explanation: Long, sunny summers ripen specialty crops while reservoirs fed by Sierra Nevada snowmelt supply summer irrigation.

trap_notes.b: Mediterranean climates have dry summers rather than daily thunderstorms.
trap_notes.c: The Central Valley rarely experiences severe subzero blizzards.
trap_notes.d: Central Valley orchards depend heavily on engineered irrigation.
trap_notes.default: Sunny dry summers paired with snowmelt irrigation create ideal orchard conditions.

prompt: Why do cities like Tokyo and San Francisco enforce strict seismic building codes despite higher costs?

options.text: Flexible steel frames absorb shaking, saving lives and cutting collapse
Thick brick walls stop tectonic plates from moving along faults
Building codes prevent underwater earthquakes from happening offshore
Tall towers anchor continental crust so bedrock cannot vibrate

explanation: Base isolation and ductile steel frames let structures sway safely during quakes, sharply reducing casualties and losses.

trap_notes.b: Unreinforced brick is brittle and collapses easily; buildings cannot stop plates.
trap_notes.c: Engineering reduces damage on land but cannot prevent tectonic earthquakes.
trap_notes.d: Towers do not anchor continental plates.
trap_notes.default: Seismic engineering helps buildings flex with ground motion rather than collapse.

prompt: Which process explains how the Colorado River carved the deep Grand Canyon over millions of years?

options.text: Tectonic uplift raised the plateau as the river cut downward
Continental ice sheets plowed a straight trench to the sea
Ocean waves eroded limestone cliffs during a single hurricane
Volcanic lava tubes collapsed along a coastal transform fault

explanation: As the Colorado Plateau rose slowly, the Colorado River maintained its grade by eroding deeper into layered rock.

trap_notes.b: Glaciers did not reach the Grand Canyon; running water carved it.
trap_notes.c: The Grand Canyon sits high inland, far from ocean storm waves.
trap_notes.d: The canyon is a fluvial erosional landform, not a collapsed lava tube.
trap_notes.default: Plateau uplift combined with steady river incision carved the canyon.

prompt: How does the ice-albedo feedback amplify warming in polar tundra and Arctic seas?

options.text: White sea ice reflects less heat than dark ocean water below
Melting bright ice exposes dark water that absorbs more sunlight
Thicker snowpack traps geothermal heat inside polar oceans
Expanding glaciers reflect solar energy back to tropical deserts

explanation: Bright ice has high albedo (reflectivity); when it melts, dark ocean or land absorbs solar energy and accelerates warming.

trap_notes.a: Bright white ice reflects far more sunlight than dark ocean water.
trap_notes.c: Arctic amplification is driven by solar absorption, not geothermal heat.
trap_notes.d: Melting, not expanding, ice drives the positive warming feedback.
trap_notes.default: Replacing reflective ice with dark water increases absorbed solar heat.

prompt: What do closely spaced contour lines on a USGS topographic map indicate about the terrain?

options.text: A flat coastal marsh near sea level
A broad floodplain with slow meanders
A steep slope where elevation rises rapidly
An arid desert plateau with no drainage

explanation: Each contour line marks a set elevation step, so packed lines show a rapid vertical change over a short horizontal distance.

trap_notes.a: Flat terrain has widely spaced contour lines.
trap_notes.b: Broad floodplains show few, widely separated contour lines.
trap_notes.d: Line spacing shows slope steepness, not rainfall or aridity.
trap_notes.default: Closely packed contour lines represent steep elevation changes.

prompt: What is a toponym in human geography?

options.text: A graph showing seasonal rainfall and temperature
A boundary line drawn along a mountain watershed
A measure of arable land per farm worker
A place name that often reflects local history or culture

explanation: Toponyms—such as Santa Fe, New Amsterdam, or Mount Rainier—preserve clues about settlers, languages, and landforms.

trap_notes.a: A graph of rainfall and temperature is a climograph.
trap_notes.b: A watershed boundary is a drainage divide.
trap_notes.c: People or workers per unit of farmland is agricultural or physiological density.
trap_notes.default: A toponym is the geographic name given to a place.

prompt: What structural problem occurs when permafrost thaws beneath roads and pipelines in subarctic regions?

options.text: Waterlogged ground loses strength, causing surfaces to buckle and sink
Thawed soil hardens into solid granite that blocks highway grading
Underground ice expands upward into tall volcanic cinder cones
Melting frost pulls coastal ocean tides inland across mountain passes

explanation: Frozen ground acts like concrete; when ice-rich permafrost melts, the mud slumps and damages foundations and roads.

trap_notes.b: Thawing softens frozen soil into unstable mud rather than granite.
trap_notes.c: Volcanic cinder cones are unrelated to frozen soil thaw.
trap_notes.d: Permafrost thaw causes local ground subsidence, not inland ocean tides.
trap_notes.default: Thawing ice-rich permafrost destabilizes soil and warps infrastructure.

prompt: Which climate pattern characterizes a tropical savanna biome such as the East African Serengeti?

options.text: Year-round freezing temperatures with stunted mosses
Warm temperatures year-round with distinct wet and dry seasons
Mild rainy winters followed by cool foggy coastal summers
Constant heavy daily downpours supporting dense closed canopy

explanation: Tropical savannas sit between rainforests and deserts, supporting grasslands and scattered trees through seasonal rains.

trap_notes.a: Year-round cold with mosses describes Arctic or alpine tundra.
trap_notes.c: Mild wet winters and dry summers define a Mediterranean climate.
trap_notes.d: Constant daily rain and closed canopies belong to tropical rainforests.
trap_notes.default: Savannas stay warm year-round and alternate between wet and dry seasons.

prompt: What distinguishes a megalopolis such as the BosWash corridor from a single metropolitan area?

options.text: It is a rural farm belt with no towns above 5,000 people
It is an isolated island port cut off from inland highways
It links multiple adjacent metro regions into one urban corridor
It is a planned capital city built inside an unpopulated desert

explanation: A megalopolis forms when expanding metropolitan areas grow together along major transport corridors like Boston-to-Washington.

trap_notes.a: Megalopolises are among the most densely urbanized corridors on Earth.
trap_notes.b: Megalopolises span broad mainland transport networks.
trap_notes.d: Forward-planned capitals like Brasilia are single cities, not merged metro chains.
trap_notes.default: A megalopolis is a chain of overlapping, interconnected metropolitan areas.

prompt: What does a country's total fertility rate measure in demographic geography?

options.text: Total tons of grain harvested per square mile of cropland
Share of citizens living inside coastal metropolitan areas
Net number of international migrants arriving each decade
Average number of children a woman is expected to bear

explanation: Total fertility rate estimates average births per woman over her lifetime; about 2.1 is replacement level in low-mortality nations.

trap_notes.a: Crop output per area measures agricultural yield, not demographic fertility.
trap_notes.b: City share of population measures urbanization.
trap_notes.c: Cross-border arrivals measure immigration, not fertility.
trap_notes.default: Total fertility rate tracks average lifetime births per woman.

prompt: Which example best illustrates stimulus diffusion?

options.text: A fast-food chain adapts its menu to local vegetarian tastes abroad
Immigrants move to a new city and open a bakery using old recipes
A wildfire spreads rapidly across dry pine trees in summer
A river carries fallen logs downstream to a coastal delta

explanation: In stimulus diffusion, the core idea spreads to a new culture, which modifies the form—like veggie burgers in India.

trap_notes.b: People carrying an intact tradition to a new place is relocation diffusion.
trap_notes.c: Wildfires are physical ecological events, not cultural diffusion.
trap_notes.d: Rivers moving logs are physical transport, not cultural spread.
trap_notes.default: Stimulus diffusion spreads an underlying concept while adapting its form locally.

prompt: In Alfred Weber's industrial location model, where should a weight-losing factory like a copper smelter locate?

options.text: Close to the raw ore mine to avoid hauling heavy waste rock
Inside the distant retail mall where finished wires are sold
At the geographic midpoint of every ocean shipping route
Along high mountain ridges far from roads and rail lines

explanation: When raw inputs are much heavier than the final product, locating near the mine minimizes total transport costs.

trap_notes.b: Market-oriented location fits weight-gaining goods like bottled beverages.
trap_notes.c: Break-of-bulk ports help when switching transport modes, not mid-ocean sites.
trap_notes.d: Factories rely on accessible rail or road transport, not remote peaks.
trap_notes.default: Bulk-reducing industries locate near raw materials to cut shipping weight.

prompt: How does a fjord form along high-latitude coastlines such as Norway or Alaska?

options.text: Coral polyps build steep limestone walls around deep lagoons
Sea-level rise floods a deep U-shaped valley carved by glaciers
Desert windstorms hollow out coastal granite cliffs above tide
River deltas pile up mud bars across flat tropical bays

explanation: Fjords are steep-walled glacial troughs that filled with ocean water when ice sheets melted and sea levels rose.

trap_notes.a: Coral reefs grow in warm tropical seas, not cold high-latitude coasts.
trap_notes.c: Fjords are carved by moving glacial ice, not desert winds.
trap_notes.d: River deltas build flat sediment fans rather than deep rocky inlets.
trap_notes.default: Fjords are drowned glacial valleys along formerly glaciated coasts.

prompt: Why does atmospheric pressure decrease as a hiker climbs higher up a tall mountain?

options.text: Strong mountain winds blow oxygen downward into deep caves
Rock strata at high elevations absorb nitrogen out of the air
Less air column remains overhead to press down on the surface
Snowfields freeze air molecules into solid crystals at the summit

explanation: Air pressure equals the weight of overlying air; higher altitudes have thinner air and lower pressure, causing cooler temperatures.

trap_notes.a: Winds redistribute air horizontally rather than pushing oxygen into caves.
trap_notes.b: Mountain rocks do not strip nitrogen from the atmosphere.
trap_notes.d: Nitrogen and oxygen stay gaseous at mountain summit temperatures.
trap_notes.default: Higher elevation means less atmosphere above, lowering air pressure and density.

prompt: Why do some countries move their seat of government to a forward capital like Brasilia or Abuja?

options.text: To relocate parliament onto a floating offshore oil platform
To keep foreign tourists from visiting historic coastal harbors
To abandon all road and rail links across the national interior
To spur interior development and balance regional political power

explanation: Forward capitals shift administration away from crowded colonial coastal ports to integrate interior regions.

trap_notes.a: Forward capitals are built on mainland interior sites, not oil platforms.
trap_notes.b: Coastal cities like Rio de Janeiro remain major tourism and trade hubs.
trap_notes.c: Forward capitals require new highways and airports to link the interior.
trap_notes.default: Forward capitals promote interior growth and reduce coastal dominance.

prompt: Why do lines of longitude converge at the poles while lines of latitude stay parallel?

options.text: Meridians are great-circle halves meeting at the poles; parallels ring East-West
Latitude lines curve inward to avoid crossing the Equator
Earth's oceans pull longitude lines closer near the Equator
Cartographers draw meridians slanted to match trade-wind paths

explanation: North-south meridians run from pole to pole and meet there, whereas east-west parallels stay equidistant from the Equator.

trap_notes.b: Latitude lines run parallel to the Equator and never cross it.
trap_notes.c: Longitude lines are widest apart at the Equator, not pulled closer there.
trap_notes.d: Meridians follow true north-south geometry, not wind belts.
trap_notes.default: Meridians meet at Earth's poles while parallels remain evenly spaced circles.

prompt: What does crop rotation between corn and soybeans help farmers maintain in Midwest soils?

options.text: Subsurface permafrost layers that prevent summer drought
Soil nitrogen fertility and lower pest pressure without fallow years
Saltwater marshes suited for growing coastal mangrove trees
Steep volcanic terraces that block wind across flat prairies

explanation: Soybeans host bacteria that fix atmospheric nitrogen into soil, replenishing nutrients used by corn and breaking pest cycles.

trap_notes.a: Iowa has temperate prairie soils without permafrost.
trap_notes.c: Midwestern farms rely on freshwater rain, not coastal saltwater marshes.
trap_notes.d: Midwestern prairies are flat or gently rolling, not volcanic terraces.
trap_notes.default: Alternating legumes with grain restores nitrogen and disrupts crop pests.
